headline: Christian Bale Opens Foster Village Designed to Keep Siblings Together
meta_description: Actor Christian Bale has opened Together California, a foster care village in Palmdale with 12 housing units dedicated to keeping siblings from being separated.
summary_short: Christian Bale's long-dreamed foster care project opens in California, addressing the state's struggle to keep siblings together in the system.
body:
Christian Bale has realized a personal mission by opening Together California, a foster care village in Palmdale, California, built with one urgent purpose: preventing siblings from being torn apart by the state system. The facility spans 11,000 square feet across a 4.67-acre property and includes 12 fully-furnished housing units designed to keep families intact during their most vulnerable moments. "Imagine the absolute pain and the trauma of losing your parents or being torn from your parents, and then losing your brothers and sisters on top of that," Bale said when announcing the project years ago. "That's no way to treat kids."

The actor and his wife Sibi discovered the scale of this problem after the birth of their first daughter, when they began researching California's foster system—the largest in the nation. They learned that most siblings entering care are routinely separated, a practice Bale felt compelled to change. The vision required substantial community support: the Austrian American Council West raised over $9 million toward the project, while philanthropist Leonardo DiCaprio also contributed. UCLA Professor and co-founder Eric Esrailian credited Los Angeles County Supervisor Kathryn Barger with championing the initiative in the Antelope Valley region.

At the ribbon-cutting ceremony, Bale reframed the work ahead: "It's our job to turn their heartbreak and their pain into love and hope and a sense of future." With LA County holding more children in foster care than any other American county, Together California represents a concrete step toward what Bale calls a "holistic, loving, and long-term approach" to child welfare.
quick_facts: 12 fully-furnished housing units across 11,000 square feet
Located on 4.67-acre property in Palmdale, California
Austrian American Council West raised over $9 million
Addresses California's largest foster care system in the nation
